title: Contextual Quality Thermostat for Shadow and Canary Traffic
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement a 'quality thermostat' that continuously measures a composite quality temperature for staged rollouts (shadow, canary, and split/A-B) using weighted eval prompt sets. The thermostat should: 1) compute a single quality metric per rollout segment composed of multiple eval signals (scorecard pass rates, semantic similarity to golden outputs, calibration/entropy drift, hallucination heuristics), 2) apply contextual weighting by prompt-topic coverage and customer segmentation, 3) drive automated actions (alert, quarantine, partial rollback, full rollback) with hysteresis and manual override, and 4) expose tooling on Console for per-rollout visibility and post-mortem analysis.
acceptance_criteria: A single composite quality 'temperature' is produced every minute for each rollout segment
Configurable weights for scorecard components can be set per-project and per-customer segment
Thermostat triggers three action tiers: notify + tag, quarantine (stop promotion and divert traffic to baseline), and auto-rollback (revert traffic to pinned model)
All actions are auditable in Console with links to the underlying eval prompts, diff visualizations, and the rollback PR/commit
End-to-end test simulating a synthetic regression causes deterministic quarantine then rollback under configured thresholds
steps: Design composite metric schema (score components + normalization + decay window)
Instrument eval prompt sampling across shadow/canary traffic and tag request context for customer-segmentation
Implement thermostat service that consumes eval signals, computes temperature, and evaluates hysteresis rules
Wire thermostat to rollout controller to emit actions via existing rollout API (notify/quarantine/rollback)
Add Console pages: per-rollout temperature timeline, prompt coverage heatmap, per-prompt deltas
Add integration tests and chaos test to validate no false-positive rollbacks under noisy signals

notes: Design decisions: use weighted aggregation rather than single threshold per signal to reduce false positives from noisy metrics.
Sampling strategy: prioritize golden prompt coverage for high-impact customers and stratified random sampling for general traffic.
Fallback behavior: when rollout-controller is unreachable, thermostat will persist last-known safe action and continue emitting alerts but will not auto-rollback.
Operational runbook: drafted initial runbook for on-call to triage thermostat alarms and perform manual rollbacks if required (link in attachments).
Open questions: whether to persist full anonymized prompt/response pairs for 90 days for post-incident forensics; proposed redaction-by-default with opt-in full retention for enterprise contracts.
